title: Resume handshake with delta-suppression and idempotent chunk tokens for SSE streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a server-side resume handshake for SSE-based streaming responses that minimizes duplicate message delivery using delta-suppression heuristics, compact idempotent chunk tokens, and a lease-backed checkpoint window. The goal is to provide robust reconnect behavior across our hosted API and private deployments while preserving tool/function-call atomicity and structured output boundaries.
tasks: Draft handshake message schema (resume_token, last_seq, lease_expiry, checksum, semantic_boundary_hint)
Implement server-side checkpoint manager that emits lease-backed checkpoints and compact chunk tokens
Add delta-suppression engine to avoid re-sending stable prefix deltas for already acknowledged progress
Extend client SDKs (JS/Go/Python) to perform resume negotiation and local de-dupe using token+seq
Define compatibility shim for HTTP EventStream / JSONL clients that don't support SSE 'id' semantics
Write integration tests covering partial-functioncall replays, structured JSON output reassembly, and expired-lease behavior
Add dashboards (resume-success-rate, duplicate-chunk-rate, resume-latency) and alerting thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Server emits checkpoints with stable resume_token and lease_expiry; tokens are <= 32 bytes when base64-encoded
Client can reconnect and resume without duplicating finalized function_call frames in 99.9% of tests
If lease expired, server sends explicit 'resume_not_found' event and client falls back to full re-request
Structured JSON outputs are reassembled with preserved tool/function-call atomicity (no half-function outputs)
No regressions on existing non-resumable streaming behavior (feature flag gated rollout available)
decision_log: 2026-02-11: Chose lease-backed checkpoints (short TTL 30s) over indefinite tokens to simplify memory footprint in hosted infra
2026-02-14: Agreed to keep token format opaque to clients; clients treat tokens as lease-bound opaque strings
2026-02-17: Delta-suppression will operate only on confirmed prefix segments (not speculative generations) to avoid semantic loss
2026-02-20: Opted for a graceful compatibility shim that maps 'event: message' JSONL lines to SSE idempotency tokens for older clients
comments: Aisha (2026-02-12): Prototype checkpoint format in runtime branch 'resume-lite' and validated compact token generation on CPU 3x faster than prior approach.
Jorge (2026-02-15): Review: need clearer retry backoff guidance in client SDK, and ensure SDK exposes opt-out for delta-suppression when deterministic replays required.
PM (Renee Liu) (2026-02-16): Customer impact: medium for integrations relying on streaming tool calls. Add opt-in toggle for enterprise Private customers during migration window.
Infra (Marco Chen) (2026-02-18): Note: checkpoint lease eviction must be observable; propose metrics resume_lease_evictions_total and resume_memory_usage_bytes.
Aisha (2026-02-21): Implemented server-side checkpoint eviction and added resume_token rotation; pushing PR for initial review: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1284
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged behind 'sse_resume_v2' for hosted and dedicated clusters
Canary rollout to 1% of traffic with duplicate-chunk alert enabled
Enterprise Private customers can enable in console per-deployment
Graceful fallback: if resume fails, client falls back to full non-resumable request with telemetry logged
notes_for_qa: Simulate flaky network with client reconnects at 50ms, 200ms, 2s intervals and verify no duplicate function_call events
Force lease expiry mid-stream and assert server returns 'resume_not_found' event and client retries cleanly
Validate compatibility shim by replaying JSONL-only client and verifying idempotent mapping to resume tokens
